questions.question_text: What values can a condition evaluate to in Python?
Which operator checks if two values are equal?
What is the difference between `=` and `==`?
Which symbol means "not equal"?
Fill in the blank: `if coins ___ 10:` means "at least 10 coins".
What must come at the end of an `if` line in Python?
Why must code inside an `if` block be indented?
options: So Python knows which lines belong to the if

questions.question_text:
What does this print?

```python
temperature = 30
if temperature > 25:
    print("It is hot out!")
```

What does this print?

```python
temperature = 20
if temperature > 25:
    print("It is hot out!")
print("Drink water")
```
When does the `else` block run?
options: When the if condition is True
When the if condition is False

questions.question_text:
What does this print?

```python
raining = False
if raining:
    print("Bring an umbrella!")
else:
    print("No umbrella needed.")
```

What does this print?

```python
coins = 15
if coins >= 20:
    print("You can buy ice-cream!")
else:
    print("You need to get more coins")
```
options: You need to get more coins
